note: The widescreen menu pack (tex-menu-wide): per page how its sides were made. Built by tools/menu-wide.py from the masters (the image model's own outputs, kept in the pack's release, not here) and the 4:3 menu pack. The model calls cannot be repeated byte for byte (no seed; the model changes under its name); everything after them is deterministic and recorded here: the canvas, the prompt as sent, the affine that aligns the master (found once by template matching and ECC, then pinned), the seam treatment and the upscaler. docs/hd-textures.md, The widescreen menu pack.

pack.name: I26 Wide
pack.aspect: 16:9 and 21:9 sides for the 4:3 menu pack's pages (the 4:3 page itself is the 4:3 pack's, untouched)
pack.licence: non-commercial; derived from Interstate '76 art, requires an owned copy of the game; the sides were drawn by an image model (Gemini 3 Pro Image, Google) from the 4:3 pages
attribution: I26 Wide: the sides of the 4:3 menu pack's pages for 16:9 and 21:9 windows.
The sides were drawn by Gemini 3 Pro Image (Google), given each 4:3 page; its outputs carry Google's SynthID watermark.
They were re-upscaled through 4xTextures_GTAV_rgt-s_dither by Philip Hofmann (CC BY 4.0, https://openmodeldb.info/models/4x-Textures-GTAV-rgt-s-dither), the 4:3 pack's own model.
Derived from Interstate '76 art: non-commercial, for owners of the game, with I26.
Recipe: tools/hd-recipes/menu-wide.json in the I26 fork's repository; the masters are in this pack's release.

shellbg1.what: Build and repair form (the trip's garage)

16x9.prompt: This is the background of a 1970s video game menu: a printed 1970s auto shop form ("BUILD AND REPAIR FORM") on aged ochre manila paper. It is being widened from 4:3 to 16:9 for widescreen monitors. The image is the full 16:9 canvas (2048 x 1152): the middle part, from x 256 to x 1792, is the real original artwork and stays exactly as it is, same position and scale; the smooth blurred colour bands at the left (x 0-256) and right (x 1792-2048) are only placeholders, to be painted over, so that the picture continues seamlessly across the two vertical joins. The finished picture: one continuous sheet of aged ochre manila paper filling the whole width. In the new areas the paper simply continues outward with exactly the same ochre colour, brightness, fibre grain and fine scan noise as the paper next to the joins, with only faint mottled stains like the ones it already has. The form's printing stops where it stops now: the new areas are blank paper. No lines, no boxes, no rules, no text, no numbers, no second form, no sheet edge, no fold, no shadow, no vignette, no border.
